kwp_installed.name: Installed capacity
kwp_installed.description: Nameplate DC capacity of PV plant
kwp_installed.source: Averta Excel model — Ejemplo 100 kW v2.86
kwp_installed.notes: Standardized ~100 kW nominal. Actual sizing per rooftop.

pvgis_yield_correction.name: PVGIS yield correction factor
pvgis_yield_correction.description: Residual gap after zone-specific PVGIS calibration. Field correction for soiling, shading, mismatch.
pvgis_yield_correction.source: Calibrated from zone-specific PVGIS data (was 0.82 pre-zone data, now 0.98 post-calibration)
pvgis_yield_correction.notes: Universal across zones. Applied after PVGIS P50 specific yield.

degradation_rate.name: Annual degradation rate
degradation_rate.description: Year-over-year production decline from panel aging
degradation_rate.source: Averta Excel model (0.35%/yr). Industry range 0.3-0.7% for mono-Si
degradation_rate.notes: Low single-year impact but compounds over 25 years. Year 25 at 0.35%: 91.7% of year 1.

curtailment_factor.name: Curtailment / sin-excedentes cap
curtailment_factor.description: Fraction of production lost to grid injection limits
curtailment_factor.source: Averta projects operate con excedentes (Alfe, Mecanizados). Pandrol sin excedentes.
curtailment_factor.notes: Sin excedentes: inverter throttles when production > consumption → lost kWh. Con excedentes: surplus injected to grid → compensated at pool price. Most new projects likely con excedentes. Model both modes.

consumer_occupancy_rate.name: Consumer occupancy rate
consumer_occupancy_rate.description: Fraction of community slots filled with paying consumers at any time
consumer_occupancy_rate.source: Target — 95% initial fill assumes pre-commercialised communities
consumer_occupancy_rate.notes: Occupancy < 100% means some solar production has no buyer → becomes surplus (valued at pool price, much lower than PPA discount revenue). Raised from 0.90 to 0.95 (2026-03-03). Assumes pre-sold communities with signed adhesion contracts before deployment. Churn risk is the #2 driver after production in the sensitivity analysis.

annual_churn_rate.name: Annual consumer churn rate
annual_churn_rate.description: Fraction of consumers who leave per year (business closure, relocation, switch)
annual_churn_rate.source: Assumption. Spanish SME failure rate ~8-10%/year. Add voluntary churn.
annual_churn_rate.notes: Churn must be offset by replacement. Net churn (churn - replacement) is what matters. Platform/sponsor risk: can Averta replace churned consumers fast enough? This is the risk taxonomy's 'churn' and 'platform/sponsor' risks combined.

churn_replacement_time_months.name: Churn replacement lag
churn_replacement_time_months.description: Average months to replace a churned consumer
churn_replacement_time_months.source: Assumption — depends on Averta's commercial capacity

retail_tariff_escalation.name: Annual retail tariff escalation (blended)
retail_tariff_escalation.description: Blended year-over-year escalation of the 3.0TD tariff, derived from component-level analysis: energy (1%), peaje + cargos (4%). Weights from Eurostat nrg_pc_205_c 2024 Band IC Spain.
retail_tariff_escalation.source: Production-weighted 3-component blend (2026-03-03). Using 3.0TD 2026 BOE-sourced peaje/cargo rates × solar production profile (P3-P6 dominant): energy 85.3% × 1% + peaje 4.7% × 4% + cargos 10.0% × 4% = 1.44%. Eurostat band-average (75.9/24.1) overstates regulated weight because solar generates in P5-P6 where peaje ≈ €0.0001/kWh. See P-026 (energy) and P-027 (network) for component justification.
retail_tariff_escalation.notes:
Three tariff components with diverging structural trajectories:
1. ENERGY (85.3% of production-weighted tariff, escalation: 1%)
   - Duck curve / wholesale price cannibalization. Spain's PNIEC targets
     81% renewable electricity by 2030, adding ~7 GW solar PV annually.
     Zero marginal cost daytime generation crushes midday wholesale prices
     to zero or negative. For a 3.0TD consumer without storage consuming
     during the day, the energy component is under structural downward
     pressure. Eurostat NRG_SUP CAGR 2017-2024: +2.4% (crisis-inflated);
     pre-crisis 2017-2019: -8.1%.
   - Demand deficit compounds the effect: PNIEC requires +34% demand by
     2030 vs 2019, but actual demand growth is too slow. If demand stays
     flat while supply explodes, zero/negative price frequency increases.

2. PEAJE + CARGOS (14.7% of production-weighted tariff, escalation: 4%)
   - Massive grid investment wave. Spanish grid cannot handle renewables
     influx + electrification (EVs, heat pumps, data centres). Late 2025:
     government raised legal investment caps on grid infrastructure by 62%
     until 2030. Transmission plan: EUR 13.5B by 2030 + EUR 7.7B local
     distribution = EUR 21.2B total. These costs pass through to consumers
     via peajes.
   - If demand doesn't grow to share the EUR 21B+ burden, cost per kWh of
     grid tolls spikes further (fixed costs spread over flat demand base).
   - Eurostat NETC CAGR 2017-2024: +7.7%; 5Y 2019-2024: +9.7%.
     Conservative estimate of 4% is below observed trend.

Blended: 0.853 × 1% + 0.047 × 4% + 0.100 × 4% = 1.44%. Weights from 3.0TD 2026 BOE rates × solar production profile. Eurostat band-average (NRG_SUP/NETC = 75.9/24.1) overstates regulated weight: solar hours concentrate in P5-P6 where peajes are near zero.
Note: pool/surplus compensation (P-024) should escalate at the energy-only rate (1%), not the blended rate, since pool price is wholesale-market-linked and subject to the same cannibalization dynamics.

surplus_price_escalation.name: Surplus/pool price escalation
surplus_price_escalation.description: Year-over-year change in the compensación simplificada rate. Wholesale-market-linked — only the energy component. No peaje, no cargos.
surplus_price_escalation.source: Structural analysis (2026-03-03). Pool/surplus compensation is indexed to wholesale market price = energy component only. Unlike autoconsumo (which avoids energy + peaje + cargos), surplus has no regulated network component. Subject to full cannibalization pressure from duck curve / PNIEC solar buildout. Same basis as P-026 (energy_tariff_escalation): 1%.
surplus_price_escalation.notes: Autoconsumo avoided cost = energy + peaje + cargos (3 components, blended 1.44% via P-023). Surplus compensation = energy only (1 component, 1%). This structural asymmetry widens over time: as peajes rise at 4%, the gap between autoconsumo value and surplus value grows — reinforcing the incentive to maximise self-consumption ratio. Engine wired: averta_t uses P-023, pool_t uses P-028 (2026-03-03).

pool_compensation_price.name: Compensación simplificada rate
pool_compensation_price.description: Comercializadora rate for surplus kWh under compensación simplificada (RD 244/2019 art. 14)
pool_compensation_price.source: Robert call 2026-02-11: 'entre 40 y 50 €/MWh'. Comercializadora negotiated rate.
pool_compensation_price.notes: NOT a pool sale. Compensación simplificada: comercializadora compensates consumer for excedentes at a negotiated rate (~€40-50/MWh). Exempt from impuesto eléctrico (5.11%) and peaje de generación (€0.5/MWh). Monthly cap: compensation cannot exceed consumed-from-grid value (bill floor = €0 on energy term). RD 244/2019 art. 14. Averta nets this compensation against its discount (exact mechanism pending Elecsum).

consumer_default_rate.name: Annual consumer payment default rate
consumer_default_rate.description: Fraction of billed revenue not collected due to non-payment
consumer_default_rate.source: SEPA Direct Debit (2026-03-03). Mandatory SEPA DD enrolment at contract signature eliminates voluntary non-payment. Residual 1% covers: failed DD (insufficient funds), disputed charges, insolvency. Spanish SME baseline 2-5% reduced by automated collection mechanism.
consumer_default_rate.notes: Different from churn. Default = consumer exists but doesn't pay. SEPA DD makes non-payment an active opt-out requiring bank revocation, not a passive failure to pay. Contract allows service suspension after 2 missed payments. Multi-offtaker structure means single default is small % of revenue. Reduced from 3% to 1% (2026-03-03).
